extracted.intended_audience: authors (research mathematicians) submitting manuscripts to Inventiones mathematicae
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on publication routes, fees, licensing, and funder-compliance when publishing papers in the journal Inventiones mathematicae (Springer Nature). Covers subscription vs open access choices, APCs, funding agreements, and Creative Commons licence options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing options (hybrid journal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventiones mathematicae is a hybrid journal. Once the article is accepted for publication, authors will have the option to choose how their article is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both subscription and open access routes are offered after acceptance. Authors should be prepared to select one of these routes at acceptance; the journal will offer both options and support choosing the correct route where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription publishing model
rubrics_metrics.description: Published articles are made available to institutions and individuals who subscribe to Inventiones mathematicae or who pay to read specific articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No APC charges apply under the subscription model. However this route isn’t suitable if funders require immediate open access because subscription authors must warrant they haven’t already committed to terms inconsistent with the journal’s licensing agreement, including any embargo period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access publishing model
rubrics_metrics.description: When an article is accepted for publication, the author(s) or funder(s) pay an article processing charge (APC). The final version of the published article is then free to read for everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must select open access publication to comply with funder mandates that require immediate access (examples given: NIH, Plan S members). Springer Nature will help authors choose the correct route where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder and institutional open access compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may need to take specific actions to achieve compliance with funder and institutional open access mandates; some funders (for example NIH or Plan S members) require immediate accessibility on publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your funder requires immediate access you need to select open access publication. Check funder/institution licence requirements and use available guidance from Springer Nature to meet those requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author warranty regarding prior commitments and embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription authors must warrant that they haven’t already committed to terms inconsistent with the journal’s licensing agreement, including the embargo period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have previously committed to terms that preclude the journal’s license or impose conflicting embargoes, the subscription route may not be available; consider selecting open access to meet funder mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee (APC) requirement and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who publish open access in Inventiones mathematicae are required to pay an article processing charge (APC). The APC price will be determined from the date on which the article is accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current APC listed: £2290.00 GBP / $3190.00 USD / €2590.00 EUR. The fee is subject to VAT or local taxes where applicable. Visit the open access support portal and Journal pricing FAQs for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding or reducing APCs via subscription route or agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can choose the subscription publishing model (no APC charges apply); Springer Nature also offers agreements that enable institutions to cover open access publishing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select your institution to check eligibility for institutional agreements. Authors may also be eligible for open access funding via their research funders or institutions—see Springer Nature’s open access funding and support services for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access funding and institutional agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature offers agreements that enable institutions to cover open access publishing costs and authors may access open access funding directly from funders and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the publisher’s tools to check whether your institution is part of an agreement that covers APCs. Consult the open access support portal for steps to apply institutional or funder coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons licences for open access articles (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access articles in Springer Nature journals are published under Creative Commons licences. These provide an industry-standard framework to support easy re-use of open access material. Under Creative Commons licences, authors retain copyright of their articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventiones mathematicae articles are published under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 or CC BY 4.0. Authors should review licence terms and consider licence variations to meet funder or institutional requirements; see the publisher’s guide to licensing, copyright and author rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: CC BY-NC-ND licence (Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article can be shared for non-commercial purposes as long as the authors are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission is needed for commercial re-use or sharing adapted and derivative versions. Choose this licence if funder/institution allows or requires it, and if you do not want derivatives or commercial reuse without permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: CC BY licence (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article may be shared and adapted for any purpose, including commercially, so long as the authors are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This licence allows maximum reuse and adaptation; use it when funders or your institution require CC BY (for example many Plan S policies) or when you want to permit commercial reuse and derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of publishing open access
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing open access offers a number of benefits, including greater reach and readership: OA articles have on average more citations, more downloads, and greater Altmetric attention (specific multipliers are given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics cited: 1.6x more citations, 4x more downloads, 2.5x more Altmetric attention; OA articles attracted 1.9x more news mentions and 1.2x more policy mentions. Consider these benefits when deciding between OA and subscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licence variation and meeting funder/institution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You may wish to find out about licence variations that are available to meet funder and institutional open access licence requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the publisher’s guide to licensing, copyright and author rights for journal articles to determine available licence options and ensure compliance with funder/institution mandates.
